label: Move
source: A move as the lines it adds: the state changes (so the state tax does), every needs line scales by the cost-of-living index of the destination against where you are, and the move itself leaves cash once (data/moving_cost.json, the regional band). The state index is a reading of MERIC's cost-of-living index by state, national = 100, rounded.
confidenceNote: A state index hides the city inside it; a move from one city to another in the same state can swing more than the state figure. A real rent quote beats the index every time.
note: Read by shared/blocks.js (D-178). `questions` are the block's four answers at most. Each `lines[]` entry is a DAITE delta: `path` must resolve under debt / assets / income / taxes / expenses; `delta` is an expression in the shared language (shared/expr.js): @answer, $household figure, {table} lookups. `when` (optional) is a condition that must hold for the line to exist. `source` is national unless `stateSource` resolves to a value for the answer's state, then state; `user` when the figure is the household's own. No expansion logic lives in a room. 15.6 (D-181): the state figures come from data/states.json through the statesByCode view; the block keeps no copy.

lines.label: The state changes
lines.note: State income tax follows the new state.

lines.label: Every needs line scales
lines.note: Destination over origin, less one: a share on each needs line. The destination is a city index (data/col_index.json) when one is named, else the state index; the origin is YOUR state’s index, because that is the one thing the household already knows and a block asks four answers at most. The move event in What If asks your city too; both read the destination from the same table row. D-267.
